today.h: The CPI Reckoning: a Hot Print Re-Arms the Rate Trade — and the AI Complex Pays
today.c1: The CPI reckoning arrived: September inflation ran at 3.7% y/y (core 2.6%) — hotter than the 3.6% consensus — and the market repriced the Fed in real time: October hike odds jumped to ~37% from ~22%, December to ~91%. The 10Y spiked to 5.33% and the 30Y to 5.63%; the dollar hit its highest since May 2025. The pain landed where duration lives: CoreWeave -15.5% (its bonds trading at distress levels; its CEO called the market 'irrational'), Oracle -8.8%, Dell -11.3% on a Barclays downgrade, Nebius -10.1%, AMD -5.7%, Nvidia -3.2% — and the chip gauge's six-day drop reached ~12%. The Nasdaq closed -1.88% at 26,692.87 — its worst day since July 23 — and the S&P fell 1.11% to 7,718.94, its first 1% drop in more than 50 sessions; the Russell 2000 fell 1.9%, entering a correction. The split was the tell: eight of 11 sectors fell, but defensives bid — health +2.5%, staples +2.2% — leaving the Dow just -0.09%, while Apple +0.5% closed above a $5T market cap. Banks bled on earnings day two: BofA -4.8% on a $1.2B Treasury fine and a revenue miss. The bond market round-tripped — after the CPI spike, the afternoon equity slide pulled money back into Treasuries: the 10Y closed 5.19% (-3bp) and the 30Y 5.53% (-4bp). Oil gained as the Houthis hit Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters and the IEA warned the diesel squeeze will last into 2027 — WTI +1.0% to $95.09 (a three-week high), Brent +0.4% to $106.06 — and the Beige Book said fuel costs are 'permeating all District reports.' Gold fell 1.6% to $4,108.60; bitcoin ~$81.7k (-1.7%). Next: PPI, retail sales and TSMC.
today.c4:
• CPI passed the baton to the Fed: October (Oct 27-28) now prices ~37% and December ~91% — with PPI and retail sales Thursday and Warsh in Bangkok, the rate axis keeps trading, and the AI complex stays its highest-beta expression.
  • Watch the bond reversal: yields closed lower as stocks slid — if Treasuries keep absorbing equity risk the shock stays contained; if the long end re-arms above 5.3%, the AI complex gets repriced again.
  • Earnings remain the referee: TSMC Thursday is the next AI-demand test, and after Barclays' Dell downgrade, watch whether the enterprise-hardware selloff spreads.

chains.t: ① Hot CPI, Cold Tape: the Rate Shock Lands on the AI Complex
steps: The print: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected — the fastest since May — with core at 2.6% (vs 2.5%); gasoline +34.2% y/y as the war's fuel shock fed through
The repricing: October hike odds jumped to ~37% from ~22% (CME), December to ~91%; traders briefly priced two hikes by end-January before those bets faded
The yield shock: the 10Y spiked to 5.33% and the 30Y to 5.63% post-print; the dollar hit its highest since May 2025 (DXY 102.56); gold slid 1.6% to $4,108.60
The AI complex takes the hit: CoreWeave -15.5% (its 2032 bond yield hit 15%), Oracle -8.8%, Dell -11.3% (Barclays downgrade), Nebius -10.1%, AMD -5.7%, Nvidia -3.2%
The chip gauge slid a sixth straight session — its longest losing streak since May 2025
The index damage: Nasdaq -1.88% (worst since July 23), S&P -1.11% (worst since July 29; a fifth loss in six sessions)
chains.d: The main chain: a hot CPI re-armed the hike trade in real time — and the rate shock landed on the market's longest-duration assets, the AI complex.

news.fact: The Consumer Price Index reading indicated inflation rose 3.7% year-over-year in September, up from 3.4% in August and above the 3.6% expectation; 'core' CPI rose 2.6%, above the 2.5% consensus. Overall inflation was the highest annual rate since May, with gasoline up 34.2% over the last 12 months.

According to CME FedWatch, traders now see a 37% likelihood the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting in two weeks, up from 22% before the reading, and a 91% likelihood the central bank will lift rates at least a quarter-percentage point at its December meeting, up from 88% before the data.

Gold fell over 1% on Wednesday, extending losses for a third straight session, as a stronger-than-expected inflation reading increased US Federal Reserve rate hike bets for this month. US gold futures for December delivery fell 1.6% to $4,108.60 per ounce.

Stocks fell the most since July as a selloff in chipmakers extended a decline that was fueled by wagers the Federal Reserve will keep lifting interest rates to fight inflation. The S&P 500 snapped its longest streak without a 1% drop in over six years. The Russell 2000 entered a correction. A gauge of chip giants sank 4.3% — extending a six-day drop to about 12%; CoreWeave Inc.'s bonds hit levels that usually signal distress.

Drops of 3.2% for Nvidia, 3.1% for Broadcom and 5.7% for Advanced Micro Devices were among the day's heaviest weights on the S&P 500. CoreWeave tumbled 15.5% for its worst day since February, GE Vernova dropped 6.2%, and Oracle sank 8.8%.

Together the declines erased some $80 billion of market value. Barclays on Wednesday downgraded Dell and two other enterprise hardware stocks, noting that Dell shares have quadrupled this year — part of an AI-fueled investor binge that has resulted in 16 stocks in the S&P 500 technology sector at least doubling this year, according to Reuters calculations. Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data; a CoreWeave bond issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%.

The S&P 500 declined 1.11% to end the session at 7,718.94 points, its biggest one-day drop since July 29. The Nasdaq declined 1.88% to 26,692.87 points, its biggest daily drop since July 23. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.09% to 51,621.48 points.

chains.t: ② Earnings Day Two: the Fine, the Miss — and a Four-Month Low
steps: BofA -4.8%: EPS 91c vs $1.09 expected (the $1.2B Treasury AML/sanctions fine cost 17c), revenue $30.0B missed as investment-banking and trading revenues fell
The fine: Treasury cited a 'failure to mitigate and report priority national security risks' — more than $5B in suspicious transactions — plus a separate $11.6M sanctions settlement
Peers: Morgan Stanley -2.7% despite a profit rise (equity traders trounced estimates; record wealth inflows); State Street -4.1% on weaker revenue
The read: the S&P 500 Banks index dipped to its lowest in over four months
The counter-bid: BlackRock +0.7% on $205B of quarterly inflows; Bending Spoons +41% as Berkshire added $330M for a 4% stake
chains.d: Earnings day two: the banks' beats didn't pay either — a $1.2B fine and a revenue miss dragged the cohort to a four-month low.

news.fact: Bank of America shares finished nearly 5% lower as its results came up shy of analysts' estimates after the U.S. Treasury Department fined the firm $1.2 billion for alleged money-laundering violations. Morgan Stanley shares declined almost 3%, while BlackRock stock rose less than 1%.
Morgan Stanley's third-quarter profit climbed as the firm's equity traders trounced analysts' estimates and the wealth-management operation brought in a record amount of money.

Bank of America said it earned 91 cents per share in the third quarter, below the $1.09 analysts were looking for as the fine caused a 17 cent hit to earnings. Revenue came in at $30.0 billion, up 3% year-over-year, but short of the $30.39 billion consensus. The Treasury said its investigation uncovered a 'failure to mitigate and report priority national security risks,' including more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions; Bank of America also agreed to an $11.6 million settlement over nearly 500 'apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs' including on Russia and Iran.

Bank of America dropped 4.8% after reporting weaker profit and revenue for the summer than analysts expected. State Street sank 4.1% after reporting weaker revenue for the latest quarter than analysts expected, even though its profit was slightly above their forecasts.
The S&P 500 Banks index dipped to its lowest level in over four months.

Bending Spoons stock is soaring more than 40% Wednesday afternoon after the Italian owner of AOL and Vimeo announced that Berkshire Hathaway had increased its stake in the company to 4%. Berkshire invested a further $330 million in Bending Spoons after previously having invested $600 million at the latter's initial public offering.

chains.t: ③ The Split: Eight Red Sectors — but the Defensives Bid
steps: Sector map: healthcare +2.5% and staples +2.2% led all 11; energy +0.6% was the only other green — eight sectors closed red
The high-multiple hit: tech -3.0% and comms -1.3% at the bottom
The index spread: Dow -0.09% vs Russell 2000 -1.9% (entering a correction, ~11% below its August peak) — composition decided who bled
The Mag7 outlier: Apple +0.5% closed above a $5T market cap; the other six fell — Meta -3.3%
The read: 'traders hide in value stocks and lower-beta sectors' (Bloomberg) — a rotation, not a run
chains.d: The split: the CPI shock hit the high-multiple end — and the rotation into defensives kept the Dow at a rounding error.

news.fact: The higher-yield bogeyman has returned to haunt stocks after Wednesday morning's inflation print, prompting traders to hide in value stocks and lower-beta sectors, which are less sensitive to index gyrations. — Tatiana Darie, Macro Strategist, Markets Live

Apple rose about 0.5% to close with a market capitalization above $5 trillion. The other Magnificent Seven mega-cap tech stocks fell, and the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS), which tracks the group, declined 2%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 48 points, or 0.1%, and the Nasdaq composite slid 1.9% as stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry led the way lower.

chains.t: ④ The Barrel's Fear Trade: Aramco Hit, Diesel Warning
steps: The escalation: Houthi attacks struck Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters building (a limited fire, per the energy ministry); a container ship sank south of Hormuz after hitting a naval mine; Iran is deploying 'new tactics' against tankers
The warning: the IEA said the diesel squeeze will extend well into next year — gasoil supply falls short of demand in Q4, with inventories unlikely to refill before H2 2027
The settles: WTI +1.0% to $95.09 (a three-week high); Brent +0.4% to $106.06 — the 'fear trade' back on
The CPI tie-in: gasoline +34.2% y/y fed the print; the Beige Book says 'higher oil prices permeated all District reports,' with fuel surcharges passing through supply chains
The counter-current: expectations of more Russian diesel cap the upside; Gulf flows ex-Iran were above 81% of pre-war levels in September
chains.d: The barrel: escalation and the diesel warning vs the Russian-diesel offset — the fear trade bid, the band held.

news.fact: Oil prices rose on Wednesday after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran said it was deploying new tactics to target ships and keep oil prices high. Brent crude futures settled up 37 cents, or 0.35%, at $106.06 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 95 cents, or 1.01%, to $95.09, a three-week high.

'Constraints on the diesel market will extend well into next year,' the International Energy Agency warned on Wednesday. 'However, even with a rapid recovery expected in refinery throughputs into year-end, gasoil supply falls short of meeting demand in 4Q26, suggesting that the replenishment of lost inventories, outside of typical seasonal fluctuations, is unlikely before [the second half of 2027].'

The Saudi Ministry of Energy said Wednesday that an administrative building belonging to oil giant Saudi Aramco had been attacked overnight; no injuries were reported at the site in Dhahran, a city on Saudi Arabia's eastern coast.

A report Wednesday afternoon from the Federal Reserve added anecdotal evidence to the morning's data: 'Higher oil prices permeated all District reports,' the authors of the Beige Book said. 'Firms reported elevated diesel prices and noted that fuel surcharges were passing on increased costs throughout the supply chain.'

chains.t: ⑤ The Offsets: Bonds Absorbed It — and October Isn't a Done Deal
steps: The reversal: the morning spike gave way to a midday bond bid as equities slid — the 10Y closed 5.19% and the 30Y 5.53%, both lower on the day, while the 2Y held at 4.808% (+1bp)
The read: 'some investors rotate back into the relative safety of the bond market' (CNBC) — yields near multi-year highs found buyers
The October question: TD Securities and Principal both see a hold — 'not strong enough to revive the case for an October hike'
The demand signal: ASML posted record Q3 sales and raised its full-year outlook amid strong AI demand — yet its shares fell 3.9%, sold with the complex
The gates: PPI (+0.6% m/m expected) and retail sales Thursday; TSMC earnings; Warsh in Bangkok; the Oct 27-28 meeting
chains.d: The offsets: bonds absorbed the equity shock, the front end held — and the market still treats an October hike as a coin-flip, not a base case.

news.fact: The midday reversal came as equities sold off, with the S&P 500 dropping more than 1%, leading some investors to rotate back into the relative safety of the bond market. The 2-year Treasury yield gained more than 1 basis point to 4.808%.

'Today's report makes the chance of an October hike higher, but we still believe the Fed will hold and opt for December as the market is already doing some of the work for them,' TD Securities strategists said. Seema Shah at Principal Asset Management said markets are clearly unsettled, but the latest report is not strong enough to revive the case for an October hike.

Chip equipment maker ASML on Wednesday posted record third quarter sales and raised its full-year outlook amid strong AI demand. Investors await Taiwan Semiconductor earnings on Thursday for further confirmation of the AI boom.

On Thursday, investors will get the September reading for the producer price index, September retail sales data and weekly initial jobless claims figures. For PPI, economists polled by Dow Jones are expecting a 0.6% rise on the month and a 5.5% gain on the year.

The print does not make an October hike the base case, but it reinforces the December-hike channel that was already heavily priced after Fed minutes showed most officials still expected another increase by year-end.

ytd.h: The Bull Meets the Referee: S&P +12.76% as the 10Y's +103bp Sets the Terms
ytd.d: S&P +12.76%, Nasdaq +14.85%, Dow +7.40% with ten sessions of Q4 logged — AI and earnings carry; the 10Y's +103bp, a hot CPI and an eighth month of war tax the rest.
ytd.c1: Ten sessions into Q4 and the year's base case holds — with a new referee: the bull runs on AI capex and earnings, fighting the same two taxes — a 10Y up 103bp to 5.19% (fresh 24-year highs printed this month) and oil up ~66% as the war grinds through its eighth month — plus the year's newest twist: a hot September CPI that revived October hike odds (~37%). The scoreboard: S&P +12.76%, Nasdaq +14.85%, Dow +7.40%; underneath, Energy (+51.3%) leads the year while Consumer Discretionary (-6.6%) lags; Comms (-5.9%) and Utilities (-2.3%) also lag. Nvidia +18.7% YTD as the AI complex's repricings (memory, equipment, credit) now cut both ways. Gold -5.4% as real rates, not war, dominated; December prices ~91%.
ytd.c4:
• The year's lesson holds into Q4: buy where earnings compound (AI infrastructure), rent where rates rule — and CPI just raised the rent.
  • Rates: the 10Y's +103bp is 2026's biggest tax — a confirmed Fed pause remains the largest single bullish catalyst left this year.
  • The bull turned four (10/12) with the AI trade's fault lines visible: power, credit, competition — and now rate sensitivity.

news.fact: Tight global crude supplies during the Iran war have sent US crude soaring more than 60% so far this year, stoking inflation pressures. In response to those pressures, the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates in September for the first time since July 2023.

'Inflation is alive and the only way the Warsh Fed knows how to kill it is with another dose of higher rates,' said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. With inflation remaining sticky, the central bank may need to raise rates higher and keep them there for longer in 2027.

Bloomberg reported that OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70 billion in annualized revenue by the end of the year, helping quell worries that the AI boom is running out of steam.

Selling has been particularly intense in CoreWeave, which has issued $22 billion of bonds and $26 billion of loans, according to LSEG data. A CoreWeave bond that was issued in June yielding 9.625% recently yielded 15%.

The month's escalation: the heaviest tanker-attack week; 24 ships hit in the two weeks to 10/11; a container ship sank south of Hormuz
The storm layer: Isaias shut-ins — 62.9% of Gulf output at the peak
The policy stack: G7/IEA releases — and the Russia diesel deal (now being downplayed by its author)
chains.d: War as the norm: the barrel carries the premium — and policy carries the offsets.

news.fact: Last week already saw the biggest number of attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz since the Iran war began — cutting the number of vessels trying to get through to the lowest in more than two months.
Analysis by the Financial Times said 24 ships were hit in the two weeks to 11 October; of the vessels hit, three were refined energy product tankers and two others were crude oil tankers.
Approximately 62.9% of daily offshore oil production, or 1.28 million barrels per day, has been shut in as Hurricane Isaias strengthens.

steps: From cuts to hikes: a September hike (first since July 2023)
The odds: October ~37%, December ~91% (CME FedWatch)
The dollar +4.4% as the regime re-priced; gold -5.4% as real rates dominated
The gates: PPI and retail sales (10/15), the Oct 27-28 meeting — every print now moves the whole curve
chains.d: The regime changed in 2026: cuts became hikes, the dollar firmed — and Wednesday's CPI showed every print still prices the curve.

news.fact: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said additional rate hikes will probably be necessary, but the timing of those hikes is 'flexible.'

According to CME FedWatch, traders now see a 37% likelihood the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its meeting in two weeks, up from 22% before the reading, and a 91% likelihood the central bank will lift rates at least a quarter-percentage point at its December meeting.
